_doc: Cultivating clans part 2: Lục of Phong Đăng, the Hỗ house of Yên Ba, the Đới silk house of Tang Điền. Story: clans.md.

people.cause: marsh fever, caught clearing the last of the flooded paddies; died at 162
people.role: Cleared the first Lục paddies; the harvest of 600 (A288)
people.backstory: Lục Đa Cốc cleared the first paddies of Phong Đăng and in 600 brought in a harvest so rich that the Tower took its grain tax from the Lục first, as it has every year since (A288).

people.role: Head of the Lục of Phong Đăng: the paddies, the granaries and three hundred tenant households
people.appearance: A big, sun-darkened farmer in a straw cape over a silk robe, who weighs a handful of rice by eye and is never wrong.
people.backstory: Lục Thương Lẫm holds the paddies of Phong Đăng and the three hundred tenant households who plant them, the Thiều among them. Since Lục Đa Cốc's (luc_da_coc) harvest of 600 the Tower has taken its grain tax from the Lục first, in kind, before any other farm in the south (A288), and the Lục call it an honour in public. He formed his core at a hundred and forty on pills bought with that surplus, and on a scripture bought with a worse one: in the great drought of 1150 he sold the Lục granaries' old rice to the Tower at four times the price, and the Tower marched on Đan Sơn Mạch's cinnabar to pay him (C188). He has three sons. Lục Kế Điền (luc_ke_dien), the heir, is a hundred and forty and still at Foundation. Lục Nhị Hòa keeps the tallies beside the Tower's counters. The third, Lục Đạo Hoa (luc_dao_hoa), left the fields at twenty for Cốc Vũ Quán's spirit-rice terraces. The abbess there, Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu), was born on his grandfather's tenancy in a drought year, and he has sent her rice every autumn for a hundred and fifty years. No Lục has ever been taken into the Tower, whose gate wants Metal, because Metal is not in the family.
people.wants: A Lục inside the Tower, so that the family is counted by the Tower instead of counted first.
people.secret: In the drought of 1171 he paid the abbey's prior Thời Tri Tiết to bring rain to his own paddies only. The tenants' fields across the river stayed dry, and three Thiều children died that winter. The payment is in the prior's second receipt book.

His father, a Kết Đan with three centuries ahead of him, will outlive him by two hundred years. Every pill the family buys goes to the tax first and to him second. His wife Tống Thanh Miêu (tong_thanh_mieu) has started buying them for him herself.

people.cause: lost at sea with three ships, 1120 (age 130)
people.role: Hỗ captain who married the Thẩm daughter of Bạch Sa (A029)
people.backstory: A Hỗ captain of Yên Ba who married a daughter of the Thẩm of Bạch Sa in 1040 and built the jetty that made the white sands a trading town (A029); he was lost with three low-riding ships off the cape in 1120.

people.role: Head of the Hỗ house of Yên Ba: a coasting fleet and the port's warehouses
people.appearance: Small, quick and plainly dressed, with a counting-rod case at his belt and a sailor's habit of watching the sky while he bargains.
people.backstory: Hỗ Tế Xuyên is the son of a Hỗ sea captain, Hỗ Độ Hải (ho_do_hai), and a Thẩm girl of Bạch Sa, whose marriage in 1040 made the white sands a trading town (A029). His mother never cultivated and died at seventy. He took the house at seventy-four, when his father was lost with three ships off the cape in 1120. The Hỗ fleet carries Thúy Vi's pills for the port house at Yên Ba under Diêm Hải Tảo (diem_hai_tao), and the cape's salt, tea and timber for anyone who pays. The house has no method of its own and does not want one. Everything a Hỗ cultivates was bought, and he formed his core at a hundred and fifty on bought pills. He trusts his mother's kinsman Thẩm Tịnh Sa (tham_tinh_sa), who keeps the port house's books, more than any of his captains. In 1170 Kim Vạn Lý (kim_van_ly) offered to buy the fleet. Tế Xuyên sent him a sandalwood model of it and no reply. He sent his great-grandson Hỗ Kinh Điểu (ho_kinh_dieu) up to Vân Khởi Quán's school to be made calm.
people.wants: A Hỗ child in Thúy Vi's inner gate, which the sect does not sell and he has never stopped trying to buy.
people.secret: One ship in ten of his fleet has a second hold, and the pills in it are Lạc Đan Thanh's copies under Thúy Vi's seal. If his cousin's books are ever weighed against the cargo, the port house will know.

His grandfather Hỗ Độ Hải (ho_do_hai) was lost in a storm with ships that rode too low, and he has twice asked his father to tear the second holds out. His wife Mẫn Tú Chi (man_tu_chi) keeps the warehouses and says nothing.

people.cause: the reeling-house damp settled in her lungs; died at 167
people.role: A Hỏa Ti reeler's daughter who taught the Đới to reel (N-chuc_ha-01)
people.backstory: Nhan Dư Ti was fifteen when Hỏa Ti Trấn burned in 590 and the reelers' daughters fled to Tang Điền with the reeling songs (N-chuc_ha-01). She married a Đới cocoon-buyer and taught his house to reel. The Đới method, the Reeling Thread Breath, is her songs written down by her grandson: a breath drawn as fine and unbroken as a thread from a cocoon. She reached Foundation at sixty and never went back up the mountain.

people.role: Silk trader of Tang Điền; father of Đới Tàm Nương and Đới Liệt Cương
people.backstory: The silk trader who bought cocoons from every picker in Tang Điền for a century and fathered Đới Tàm Nương (doi_tam_nuong) and, at a hundred and five, Đới Liệt Cương (doi_liet_cuong).

people.role: Head of the Đới silk house of Tang Điền; its best reeler
people.appearance: A small, burn-scarred woman with a reeler's quick fingers and a voice that carries across the whole silk market.
people.backstory: Đới Tàm Nương is the best reeler in Tang Điền and the head of the Đới, a silk house that passes to its best reeler, son or daughter, and takes her husband into its name. The house buys cocoons from the mulberry pickers, reels them on the Reeling Thread Breath that her ancestress Nhan Dư Ti (nhan_du_ti) carried out of burning Hỏa Ti, and sells raw silk at the Tang Điền market. Two buyers matter. Chức Hà Các's weavers need Tang Điền thread for the fire-silk Thân Vân Cẩm (than_van_cam) weaves without the vents. The palace's factor Chiêm Lợi Châu (chiem_loi_chau) buys first and cheapest for Phượng Minh, and since the palace moved its seat to Hỏa Ti in 1162 he has set the price for the whole market. Her younger brother Đới Liệt Cương (doi_liet_cuong) left the house for Phần Vũ's vents to stop being a silk trader's son, and now captains the levy that guards the palace's road through the Đới mulberry fields. She has not forgiven him, and she uses him all the same.
people.wants: To sell every thread to Chức Hà and none to the palace's factor, and to live to see the factor beg.
people.secret: In her cellar she has reeled three bolts of true fire-silk, thread with fire set into it as Hỏa Ti once made it, from the old songs. The palace holds that the last fire-silk was given to its founder in 592 (N-phuong_minh-04). If it learns the Đới can make more, it will want the house, or the songs.

He thinks his mother's war with the palace will cost the house everything, and each year he sells the factor a little more than she knows. He married a mulberry picker's daughter, Long Tang Chi (long_tang_chi), and the pickers trust the Đới because of it.
